learningObjective: Interpret Nsight Compute warp stall reasons and translate them to actionable optimization steps.
stem: Nsight Compute reports the following warp stall breakdown for a custom kernel. Which conclusions and next steps are correct? (Select all that apply.)
profileData:
Kernel: my_reduce_kernel
  Warp stall breakdown (% cycles per stall reason):
    Long Scoreboard (memory latency)  : 42 %
    Barrier                            : 18 %
    Wait                               : 12 %
    Not Selected                       :  8 %
    Short Scoreboard                   :  6 %
    Others (Selected, Drain, ...)      : 14 %
  DRAM Throughput: 45 %
  L2 Hit Rate: 30 %

options.text: The dominant stall reason 'Long Scoreboard' points to memory-load latency: warps are waiting for global-memory loads. Mitigations include improving L2 hit rate (better data reuse or blocking), using async cp.async / prefetching, and increasing warps-per-SM to hide latency.

'Barrier' stall at 18% suggests __syncthreads() is taking a large fraction of time; reducing block size or eliminating synchronization is always the right response to any Barrier stall regardless of the algorithm's synchronization needs.

A 45% DRAM throughput combined with 30% L2 hit rate indicates room to reduce memory traffic (e.g., staging in shared memory) — this would attack the top stall reason at the source rather than raising occupancy to hide it.
'Long Scoreboard' means the kernel is compute-bound on the FP32 unit; warps are waiting for math to complete. The right mitigation is to add more math per thread to fill in the pipeline.

explanation: A: Long Scoreboard = waiting on global-memory loads. Latency-hiding (more warps) and reducing memory traffic are both valid mitigations. C: 45% DRAM with only 30% L2 hit rate implies workload has room to increase locality via shared-memory staging or tiling, which reduces the source of memory latency. B is wrong: Barrier stalls reflect true synchronization needs; reducing block size can hurt occupancy or algorithm correctness. D is wrong: Long Scoreboard is a memory-latency stall, not a compute stall.

optionExplanations.B: Wrong: barriers exist for correctness; removing them is not a general fix.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: reducing memory traffic attacks the root cause.

assumptions: Ampere/Hopper stall taxonomy as documented in Nsight Compute reference.
The workload is real and not measurement noise.
nonImplications: Does not imply 'Long Scoreboard' can always be eliminated; some workloads have irreducible memory latency.
Does not imply higher occupancy is always desirable.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses memory latency stall with compute stall.

performanceClaim.scope: Warp stall interpretation on Ampere/Hopper Nsight Compute output
